summary: Emmanuel Francis specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was an associate member at the University of Hamburg (attested 2013–2020) and a research fellow at the Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud (attested 2021).
Indologist Emmanuel Lang studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales under Sylvain Lévi.

Indologist Emmie te Nijenhuis studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning her PhD under Jan Gonda in 1970. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Emmy Wellesz, a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earned her PhD from the University of Vienna (1907–1921), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Josef Strzygowski.

Enamul Haque studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford (PhD). A specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology, he led the Bangladesh National Museum (1962–1991), presided over the International Council of Museums (1983–1986), and directed the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura worked in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned degrees, including a doctorate, from Kyushu University and studied at Kyoto University. His career included professorships at Kyushu University and Kumamoto University, as well as directorship of the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Buddhist studies scholar Endo Asai studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Rissho University in 1970. He held academic posts at Minobusan University, Nihon Fukushi University, and Rissho University, where he became professor in 1972 and emeritus professor in 1997.

Eng Jin Ooi studied at Universiti Sains Malaysia and earned a PhD from Mahidol University, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Chulalongkorn University, Mahidol University, and the International Buddhist College.

Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar Enga Teramoto studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held posts at Otani University as a professor beginning in 1915 and served as a lecturer at Kyoto University around 1916.

Buddhist studies scholar Enichi Ocho studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture from 1931 and served as professor and emeritus professor at Otani University from 1949 to 1976.

Enno Littmann studied at Berlin under August Dillmann, Greifswald, and Halle (PhD), also studying under Theodor Nöldeke. A scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held professorships at Princeton, Strasbourg, Göttingen, Bonn, and Tübingen (1921–1951).

Enrica Garzilli works in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at Harvard University (attested 1995), the University of Turin, the University of Perugia, ILS Law College as a lecturer, and the University of Macerata as editor-in-chief (attested 2006–2007).

Enrico Pappacena was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Naples Federico II under Michele Kerbaker, graduating by 1914. He served as professore incaricato at the University of Bari from 1946 to 1960.

Enrique Soms y Castelín specialized in Indology and linguistics. He served as professor of Greek at the University of Salamanca (ca. 1888–1913) and at the Complutense University of Madrid from 1891 to 1913.

Enryo Inoue studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara, earning a Doctor of Letters. Active in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he founded Toyo University and served as a lecturer and manager there from around 1887 to 1905.

Ensho Kanakura studied at the University of Tokyo, earning a doctorate in 1931. A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was a professor at Tohoku University and Rissho University, president of Miyagi University of Education, and a Japan Academy fellow.
Buddhist studies scholar Ensho Kobayashi has held posts at Hanazono University, serving as professor (attested 1988) and later as emeritus professor (attested 2026).
Ensho Nasu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ryukoku University under the supervision of Esho Mikogami and was a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 2007).

Enshu Kurumiya specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Australian National University in 1974 under Jan Willem de Jong, having also studied under Yukio Sakamoto, Ensho Kanakura, and Yosho Nomura, and was later a professor at Rissho University.

Entai Tomomatsu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University from around 1920 to 1923. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.
